To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
low extracellular Mg stimulates the secretion of IL8 and MCP1 in dermal endothelial cells.
low Mg activates NFκB and inhibits PPARγ, and that this interplay may be involved in the response of human dermal microvasculature to low Mg.
low magnesium induces the activation of NFκB and inhibits the activation of PPARγ in dermal microvasular endothelial cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential interplay between PPARγ and the transcription factor NFκB in dermal microvessels.
the effects of magnesium deficiency on the inflammatory response of dermal microvascular cells.
the role of PPARγ and its interplay with NFκB in dermal microvasular endothelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
low magnesium induces the activation of both PPARγ and nuclear factor κB (NFκB) in human dermal endothelial cells.
low extracellular Mg activates both PPARγ and its antagonist NFκB in human dermal endothelial cells.

low Mg stimulates the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and chemotactic factors by dermal microvascular cells via an NFκB-dependent pathway, and that PPARγ might be involved in the response to low Mg.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the low magnesium-induced NFκB activation in human dermal endothelial cells is inhibited by PPARγ.
low Mg induces a proinflammatory state in endothelial cells by stimulating the activation of NFκB and inhibiting the activation of PPARγ.
the interplay between PPARγ and the NFκB pathway in dermal microvasculature may play a role in the response of the skin to Mg deficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
low magnesium might be an important factor in the initiation of inflammatory processes in the skin.
low Mg may stimulate endothelial cells to secrete proinflammatory chemokines.
low magnesium stimulates the expression of proinflammatory mediators in dermal microvasculature, and this response might be mediated by PPARγ and/or NFκB.
